title: Installation of Livestock Holding Pens and Chutes
description: USDA�s response to the New World Screwworm (NWS) is a top priority. Its National Detector Dog Training Center (NDDTC) in Newnan, GA, is expanding its NWS training program to strengthen USDA�s operational readiness and ensure canine teams are fully prepared for field conditions. Recent pilot activities in Texas demonstrated that NWS detector dogs must be safely acclimated to livestock environments including interactions with cattle, sheep, and goats to build the skills necessary for effective detection in real?world settings. To support this requirement, NDDTC must maintain goats onsite as essential training aids. Establishing appropriate housing, fencing, shelter, and utilities is a foundational step to ensure the animals� welfare, comply with applicable standards, and provide consistent access to training environments that accurately simulate operational livestock settings. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and expertise necessary to design, construct, and install fenced livestock enclosures, shelters, flooring, utilities, water systems, and a simulated chute?training environment to support on?site goat housing and NWS canine training. All work must comply with USDA facility, animal?welfare, and safety standards and integrate with existing NDDTC infrastructure. NOTE: Quotes are required by Sept 8. Time is of the essence for this requirement as the government requires rapid delivery. The Contractor will be required to (a) commence work under this contract immediately upon receipt of the NTP, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use by October 30, 2026.. title: NOAA Oscar Sette Bridge Deck Replacement
description: This is a Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR SUBPART 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This Combined Synopsis/Solicitation 1333MK26Q0124 constitutes a Request for Quotation (RFQ) which Incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through the Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01. The National Oceanic Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Office of Marine & Aviation Operations (OMAO), Marine Operation Center (MOC), This requisition is to provide NOAA Ship Oscar Elton Sette (R 335) with Bridge Decking replacement. The solicitation is being issued as a total small business set-aside. The associated NAICS code is 336611 with a size standard of 1,300 Employees. The SCA is applicable under Wage Determination No.: 2015-5689 Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with FAR 52.212-2 Evaluation-Commercial Products and Commercial Services (Nov 2021). Your response, technical, and pricing should be forwarded electronically to the Contracting Specialist via email no later than the date and time specified above. When responding, please include the Requisition number in the subject line. To verify receipt of your response, please contact me either by email or phone. Christopher Baker Christopher.Baker@noaa.gov FIRM FIXED PRICE CLIN 0001 � BASE PoP NOAA Ship Oscar Elton Sette 1.0 INTENT: 1.1 Remove the existing tile and underlayment on the Bridge Deck of NOAA Ship Oscar Elton Sette. Prepare surface and install pre-purchased LONMARINE (LONSEAL) decking and trim. 2.0 REFERENCES: 2.1 MOC-000-1G, General Requirements for Ship Repair 2.2 Manufacturer�s Technical Data and Installation Instructions for Resilient Sheet Vinyl Deck Coverings 2.3 MIL-PRF-32584, Deck Covering Materials, Resilient (or applicable equivalent for resilient marine flooring) 2.4 Drawing No. OS-830-002, �NOAA Ship Oscar Sette General Arrangement� 2.5 LONSEAL PROFERMA INVOICE 3.0 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED MATERIALS: 3.1 LONMARINE Pre-purchased materials (LONMARINE roll, adhesive, & trim) 4.0 REQUIREMENTS: 4.1 The contractor is responsible for providing all labor, additional materials, consumables, services, tools, supervision, and technical expertise required to accomplish all work in this specification. 4.2 Engage the services of a deck coating specialist to apply the LONMARINE deck system as described in this specification (see Note 6.1). 4.3 Install protective covering to protect the vessel's equipment and to contain the dust generated by this work item within the compartment. Negative ventilation shall be maintained and exhausted to the exterior for all spaces where dust and airborne debris from work is generated. 4.4 Prove all deck drain(s) in the space to be clear and free flowing. Plug the drain(s) to preclude introduction of debris resulting from this work item. (Note: If the bridge deck does not have deck drains, this step can be removed). 4.5 Remove the existing deck material, tile, rubber cove moulding, and chip up the existing underlayment in its entirety. Remove debris from the vessel and properly dispose of it on a daily basis. 4.6 Power tool clean the entire deck, the bulkheads to a line 4 inches above the deck, as well as all foundations and interferences in accordance with Reference 2.1. Vacuum the compartment to remove all dirt and dust generated by the surface preparation activities. 4.7 Inspect the surface preparation with the COR. Inspection shall include the condition of all permanently attached fixtures in way of the deck covering installation. Submit a condition report to the COR listing deteriorated foundations or decking found during the inspection. 4.8 Upon approval of the surface preparation by the COR, apply one (1) coat of 150 zinc primer or equivalent product per flooring underlayment manufacturer's recommendations to all prepared surfaces. The primer shall be 3-4 mils DFT. 4.9 Upon approval by the COR, wipe down the primed surfaces with solvent. When dry, install ultra lightweight underlayment similar to Epmar 1290. The underlayment shall be a minimum thickness per manufacturer's recommendations, fair-in irregularities in the deck (including weld seams, depressions, etc.), and be coved up the bulkheads the lowest 4 inches. All materials shall be specifically intended for shipboard use on steel decking. 4.10 Upon inspection and approval of the underlayment by the COR, install a marine-grade resilient sheet vinyl flooring (pre-purchased Lonseal, or equivalent) in accordance with References 2.2 and 2.3. The flooring shall be installed using the manufacturer�s recommended (pre-purchased) marine-grade epoxy adhesive. Flooring shall be sloped for positive drainage to the deck drains (if applicable) and shall be flash-coved up the bulkheads 4 inches using a cove former. 4.11 All (pre-purchased) seams shall be routed and heat-welded using the manufacturers matching welding thread to create a continuous, watertight surface. The welded seams shall be skived flush with the flooring surface. 4.12 Bubbles, wrinkles, unbonded areas, telegraphing of underlayment imperfections, or poorly welded seams shall be rejected as defects. Such defects shall not be patched. Acceptable corrective action shall be the removal and re-installation of the defective sections. 4.13 Install (pre-purchased) trim against walls and bridge equipment. 4.14 Clean and paint disturbed surfaces to match the surrounding areas. Blow-down and vacuum the entire compartment. 4.15 Remove all protective covering. Clean the compartment and leave in a condition ready for use and meeting sanitary requirements (free of haze, film or other surface contamination). 4.16 Upon completion of the decking renewal, remove the drain plugs and again prove the drains to be clear and free flowing in the presence of the COR. Submit a condition report to the COR listing any drains found to be obstructed. 5.0 QUALITY ASSURANCE: 5.1 Ensure all installation, heat-welding, and materials are in strict accordance with the manufacturer�s technical instructions (Reference 2.2). 5.2 Perform a joint walkthrough inspection of the deck replacement with the COR upon completion. 5.3 Protect all new deck coverings following replacement for the duration of the contract period. New flooring that is damaged during the repair period shall be repaired or replaced at the discretion of the COR. 6.0 Notes 6.2 Contractors are encouraged to review ship�s drawings, reference documents, and submit written questions requesting any needed additional details, photos, or measurements necessary to provide an accurate bid package prior to submitting a bid proposal. For assistance in registering or for other FedConnect� questions please call the FedConnect� Help Desk at (800) 899-6665 or email at support@fedconnect.net. There is no charge for registration in or use of FedConnect�. title: Sand Trail Phase II
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 1240BJ26Q0021 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This project is located on the Cordova Ranger District. This contract aims to repair and mitigate future failures of the USFS Sand Trail infrastructure, trail number 229. The total trail length is 12.20 miles long; this contract will only address the first 1.70 miles of failing trail. The mitigation consists of installing bank armoring with rip rap, and placing sub grade aggregate along the trail. The sub grade aggregate (3� minus) is to be placed as backfill behind the riprap and is incidental to item 201501A. Backfill quantities will vary but the end product is to have ~2-4 ft of 3� minus behind the placed riprap. The D-1 aggregate is to be placed on the trail running surface to harden the trail for ATV use. The majority of trail 229 is 6 to 8 feet in width and will require additional clearing and minor excavation depending on type of equipment used. Construction must occur during low water times of year, diversion of smaller channels within the project location will be needed to dewater bank locations. Small diversion for bank armoring is assumed to be conducted with either a dozer or excavator that may operate in the stream channel or along the stream bank. Work must be performed when there is 5 consecutive days below 30F degrees are reached This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 237990 Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The small business size standard is $45,000,000.00 This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

title: B--IHNV GENOTYPING PROGRAM UPGRADE
description: The purpose of this amendment is to answer vendor questions. The period for questions is closed, and no further questions will be accepted. The due date for quotes remains the same, September 8, 2026, at 10:00am PDT. 1. How many data entries are currently in the database? approximately 3000 2. How many samples need to be added to the database from recent years? How many samples per year are being added Approximately 400. The number per year is not a set number but varies depending on field events and how many virus isolates our fish health partners to send in for genotyping. 3. Shall the previously used database stay in place? Or should the deliverables include a plan for long term database plan which may include development of a new structure/system? At this point we are aiming to update the current in-house excel database that has been in place for many years. That database will continue to be our main source of curated information. Future plans for any new system are desirable but beyond the financial scope of this contract. 4. Where (what lab) is the genotyping data being produced currently? The majority of genotyping is done at our lab, the USGS Western Fisheries Research Center, where the genotyping program originated and has been hosted since the 1990s. We also occasionally get isolate metadata and genotyped sequences from partners at the Northwest Indian Fish Commission and Oregon Department fo Fish and Wildlife. 5. What technology is being used for that? Microarray? Sanger sequencing? Next generation sequencing? Other? RNA is extracted from each virus isolate and a fragment containing the midG sequence is generated by PCR. The genotype consensus sequences are generated by Sanger or NGS either in-house or by sending the PCR fragement to a commercial sequencing service. Metadata is tracked using the in-house database that also contains the sequence generated. and the designated genotype number. 6. What is the size of each genotype that will be added or produced? Is it the full IHNV sequence or just select regions? IHNV genotypes have been established in North America using a 303 nt mid-G region that is a variable region in the virus glycoprotein (G) gene. This short region has proven robust in comparison with phylogenies based on complete G genes (1610 nt) or full genomes ( ~ 11,132 nt). It is the only sequence that facilitates phylogenetic analyses with archive of genotype data for over 3000 virus isolates that represent IHNV in all of North America. 7. What database engine does the current database use (e.g., PostgreSQL, mySQL, etc.)? The current database is a large excel file containing all metadata associated with isolates and the genotyped sequence that is associated with each isolate. 8. How many WFRC staff need to be trained annually to conduct the IHNV typing? Once staff are trained they do not need to be trained annually but as needed when any changes in the system need to be implemented. Optimally there should be two staff members who are trained to conduct the IHNV genotyping. ********************************************

title: Amendment 0001- Conex Refurbishment, Officer Training School (OTS), Maxwell AFB
description: Statement of Requirements Conex Refurbishment, Officer Training School (OTS), Maxwell AFB Purpose: The purpose of this requirement is to obtain comprehensive restoration services for 27 Conex containers located at the Vigilant Warrior (VW) training site. The restoration is necessary to eliminate significant safety hazards posed by severe wood deterioration, restore the environmental integrity of the containers, and ensure their operational effectiveness for training over 5,000 cadets annually. Description of Items: The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, and services to perform complete restoration and repair of the 27 Conex containers. The work includes, but is not limited to, the following: Structural Component Restoration Assess and replace all deteriorated wood framing, flooring, and structural elements. Ensure all replacement materials meet or exceed original load-bearing specifications and comply with military construction standard UFC 1-200-01. All structural modifications must be certified by a licensed structural engineer. Window and Door Frame Restoration Restore window and door frames to provide a complete weatherproof seal when closed. Hardware must enable secure locking mechanisms to prevent unauthorized access. Materials used must resist corrosion and deterioration in outdoor environments. Environmental Protection Systems Achieve complete weather resistance to prevent water, snow, and wind infiltration. All joints, seams, and penetrations must be properly sealed. All openings must be sealed to prevent the entry of rodents, birds, and insects. Delivery Requirements: The contractor shall provide a detailed construction phasing plan to the government for approval. The plan must ensure that a minimum of 70% of the containers remain operational at all times. No more than 12 containers may be out of service simultaneously without prior government approval. The work will be performed on-site at the Vigilant Warrior training site located in Elmore County, Alabama. The address is: 407 Lakeland Drive, Titus AL. Installation Requirements: The contractor will be responsible for the installation of all new materials and components as part of the restoration services. When material replacement is required, the contractor shall procure and install materials as per specifications approved by Officer Training School (OTS). Standard Warranty: The contractor shall provide any Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) standard commercial warranty applicable to the products being purchased at no additional cost to the Government. Warranty shall include, as a minimum, technical support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement of faulty equipment. The contractor must provide a 48-hour response for any warranty issues that affect training operations. All materials shall demonstrate a minimum 15-year service life, with a manufacturer's warranty of a minimum of 10 years on primary structural components. Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the customer with all manufacturer warranties as needed for any component incorporated into this project such as equipment manuals, literature, and other documentation on all equipment. Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the written procedures, points of contact within the company, and required information for all warranty services prior to project acceptance. This information shall include written confirmation of the warranty period, phone numbers and contact information/procedures for technical support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement of faulty equipment. General Information: Items must be brand new. Refurbished items are not authorized. Reporting: The contractor is required to provide monthly progress reports detailing progress, materials used, quality control activities, and any safety incidents. Quality Control: The contractor shall establish and maintain a Quality Control Program. A Quality Program Plan (QPP) must be submitted within 30 days of contract award. This program will include inspection hold points at 25%, 50%, and 75% completion for each container, with government inspection rights at each phase. title: NOAA: RF Generator Hardware and LabView Software for the NWS National Reconditioning Center in Grandview, MO.
description: AMENDMENT NOTICE: THE PURPOSE OF THIS AMENDMENT IS TO ADDRESS VENDOR INQUIRIES AND PROVIDE RESPONSE TO TECHNICAL QUESTIONS PER THE PROGRAM'S DIRECT INPUT. PLEASE SEE THE ATTACHED AMENDMENT DOCUMENT WITH ASSOCIATED REVISED STATEMENT OF NEED FOR REFERENCE, REVISIONS AND RESUBMISSION IF NECESSARY. THE SECONDARY PURPOSE OF THIS AMENDMENT IS TO EXTEND THE SOLICITATION ACCEPTANCE PERIOD BY AN ADDITIONAL FIVE (5) DAYS IN ORDER TO ALLOW ALL QUOTERS TO REVIEW FOR COMPLIANCE AND/OR REVISE AND RESUBMIT THEIR ORIGINAL SUBMISSIONS IF NEEDED TO REFLECT THE PROPER PRICING FOR THE REQUIRED SUPPLIES. IN ADDITION, ALL PREVIOUS QUOTERS WILL BE REQUIRED TO SIGN AND RETURN THIS AMENDMENT AS ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF THE REQUIRED CHANGES. ANY SUBMISSIONS THAT DO NOT SUBMIT A SIGNED MODIFICATION, FORM SF-30, WILL NO LONGER BE CONSIDERED FOR FURTHER CONSIDERATION DURING THE FINAL REVIEW PROCESS. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) intends to award a firm fixed price contract as a 100% small business set-aside for National Instruments RF Generator Hardware and associated LabView Software for the National Reconditioning Center in Grandview, MO. The Government intends to make an award to the responsive responsible quoter providing the best value in accordance with FAR12.203(c)(2). Brand Name Justification: This is a Brand Name Requirement. Vendors must be an authorized reseller of National Instruments LabVIEW Professional Development System. This particular brand name is essential to the requirement and market research indicates similar products do not meet or cannot be modified to meet agency needs. The National Reconditoning Center has standardized its automated test sofware development environment on National Instruments LabVIEW Professional Development System. To achieve the precise synchronization, signal generation, and measurement analysis required for diagnostic RF testing, the hardware layer must interface seamlessly with this software environment. National Instruments hardware is peculiar to this manufacturer because it utilizes proprietary, native hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) driver extensions and application programming interfaces (APls) designed explicitly for LabVIEW. Introducing an alternative ("or equal") hardware manufacturer would break this integrated ecosystem. Completing this requirement with non-NI hardware would require the agency to develop extensive custom software drivers and Dynamic Link Libraries (DLLs) simply to establish basic communication with the chassis and specialized modules. This would introduce significant risk of timing, phase, and latency mismatches during critical signal generation and analysis phases handled by the Vector Signal Transceiver (VST). Consequently, opting for an alternative brand would result in severe project delays (estimated at 6 to 12 months) and extensive additional engineering labor and costs to write, test, and validate an entirely new alternative equipment topology. Utilizing exact National Instruments hardware ensures immediate software deployment, system reliability, and standard compliance across the agency's testing infrastructure. No award can be made to a company not registered in SAM. Contractors active in SAM have a unique entity identifier (UEI) that is used to do business with the federal government. The Government has moved to a free new, non- proprietary identifier that will have to be requested in, and assigned by, the System for Award Management (SAM.gov). You can register and access the site by going to www.sam.gov. Please see Instructions to Offerors and full Solicitation as attached. **Contractors who do not respond to items 1 through 9 included in the "Instructions to Offerors" may be considered non-compliant with the requirements of the solicitation and no further consideration shall be given for award.

title: Conex Refurbishment, Officer Training School (OTS), Maxwell AFB
description: Statement of Requirements Conex Refurbishment, Officer Training School (OTS), Maxwell AFB Purpose: The purpose of this requirement is to obtain comprehensive restoration services for 27 Conex containers located at the Vigilant Warrior (VW) training site. The restoration is necessary to eliminate significant safety hazards posed by severe wood deterioration, restore the environmental integrity of the containers, and ensure their operational effectiveness for training over 5,000 cadets annually. Description of Items: The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, supervision, materials, equipment, tools, and services to perform complete restoration and repair of the 27 Conex containers. The work includes, but is not limited to, the following: Structural Component Restoration Assess and replace all deteriorated wood framing, flooring, and structural elements. Ensure all replacement materials meet or exceed original load-bearing specifications and comply with military construction standard UFC 1-200-01. All structural modifications must be certified by a licensed structural engineer. Window and Door Frame Restoration Restore window and door frames to provide a complete weatherproof seal when closed. Hardware must enable secure locking mechanisms to prevent unauthorized access. Materials used must resist corrosion and deterioration in outdoor environments. Environmental Protection Systems Achieve complete weather resistance to prevent water, snow, and wind infiltration. All joints, seams, and penetrations must be properly sealed. All openings must be sealed to prevent the entry of rodents, birds, and insects. Delivery Requirements: The contractor shall provide a detailed construction phasing plan to the government for approval. The plan must ensure that a minimum of 70% of the containers remain operational at all times. No more than 12 containers may be out of service simultaneously without prior government approval. The work will be performed on-site at the Vigilant Warrior training site located in Elmore County, Alabama. The address is: 407 Lakeland Drive, Titus AL. Installation Requirements: The contractor will be responsible for the installation of all new materials and components as part of the restoration services. When material replacement is required, the contractor shall procure and install materials as per specifications approved by Officer Training School (OTS). Standard Warranty: The contractor shall provide any Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) standard commercial warranty applicable to the products being purchased at no additional cost to the Government. Warranty shall include, as a minimum, technical support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement of faulty equipment. The contractor must provide a 48-hour response for any warranty issues that affect training operations. All materials shall demonstrate a minimum 15-year service life, with a manufacturer's warranty of a minimum of 10 years on primary structural components. Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the customer with all manufacturer warranties as needed for any component incorporated into this project such as equipment manuals, literature, and other documentation on all equipment. Prior to project acceptance, the contractor shall provide the written procedures, points of contact within the company, and required information for all warranty services prior to project acceptance. This information shall include written confirmation of the warranty period, phone numbers and contact information/procedures for technical support, troubleshooting assistance, and replacement of faulty equipment. General Information: Items must be brand new. Refurbished items are not authorized. Reporting: The contractor is required to provide monthly progress reports detailing progress, materials used, quality control activities, and any safety incidents. Quality Control: The contractor shall establish and maintain a Quality Control Program. A Quality Program Plan (QPP) must be submitted within 30 days of contract award. This program will include inspection hold points at 25%, 50%, and 75% completion for each container, with government inspection rights at each phase. title: Design-Build & Design-Bid-Build Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity Firm-Fixed-Price Multiple Award Construction Contract, NAVFAC SE Area Of Operations and anywhere in the US, focused on Naval Air Station Jacksonville & Naval Station Mayport, FL
description: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Southeast (NAVFAC SE) has been tasked to develop, solicit and award a competitively negotiated Design-Build (DB) and Design-Bid-Build (DBB) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) for new construction, renovation, and demolition for general construction projects in NAVFAC SE Area of Operations and anywhere in the US, focused on NAS Jacksonville, FL, and NS Mayport, FL. A Sources Sought Notice for this requirement was posted on SAM.gov under solicitation N69450-25-R-JMMC on August 26, 2025, requesting small business industry interest and capability statements. Based upon responses from the Notice, the Government concluded that there was enough evaluated small businesses that could meet the minimum requirements and qualifications. Accordingly, the Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued as a competitive small business set aside. All responsible small businesses with the specialized experience and qualifications required by the RFP may submit a proposal to be considered by the Agency. The NAICS code for this IDIQ MACC solicitation is 236220, with a size standard of $45,000,000 ($45M). The Government intends to award approximately ten (10) contracts resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offerors whose proposals represent the best value after evaluation in accordance with the factors and their relative importance in the solicitation. Each MACC will have a duration period of five (5) years or an aggregate maximum not-to-exceed (NTE) amount of $249,000,000 ($249M) for all contracts, whichever comes first. Task orders will be firm-fixed-priced, with a minimum value of $350,000 and a maximum value of $10,000,000 ($10M); however, task orders under or over these amounts may be considered if deemed to be in the Government�s best interest. Construction projects are planned to be issued as task orders under the MACCs. The work to be performed consists of general building-type projects (new construction, renovation, and demolition) including but not limited to: aviation and aircraft facilities; warehouse, supply, and other industrial facilities; barracks, dormitories, and personnel housing facilities; administrative facilities; training facilities; personnel support and service facilities; maintenance facilities; research facilities; commissaries and retail; medical facilities; waterfront facilities; and other similar types of facilities. Projects may require either single discipline or multi-discipline (more than 3 major design disciplines) design services or may include 100% construction performance specifications. Projects may be based on design-build, modified design-build, or full plans and specifications format and may also require comprehensive interior design and incorporation of sustainable features. The source selection method to be used is a best value continuum process in a negotiated, two-phase acquisition utilizing the trade-off approach. Formal two-phase source selection will be used to select the proposals that provide the best value to the Government from a technical and price standpoint. In accordance with FAR Subparts 15.103 and 15.202, a trade-off approach to source selection will be used for this solicitation with respect to the initial award. Offerors selected to proceed to Phase Two will be required to submit technical and price proposals for a seed project task order, which will be identified prior to entering into Phase Two. Offerors who fail to submit technical and price proposals will not be considered for an award. The offeror with the best value proposal for the seed project will be awarded an IDIQ contract under the MACC and the seed project task order, subject to funding availability. The remaining selected offerors will be awarded an IDIQ contract under the MACC and a minimum guarantee task order of $1,000.00. This will be an electronic solicitation, which will be posted to Contract Opportunities on the SAM.gov website via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. The solicitation will be available no earlier than 15 days after this pre-solicitation notice is posted. A Pre-Proposal Conference and Site Visit will be held for those offerors chosen to participate in Phase Two, with the exact date and time specified in the Phase Two solicitation. Offerors are responsible for checking the SAM.gov website for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments that may be issued. NO CONTRACT AWARD WILL BE MADE TO ANY CONTRACTOR THAT IS NOT REGISTERED OR IN THE PROCESS OF REGISTERING WITH THE SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM). PLEASE VISIT THE SAM WEBSITE AT https://www.sam.gov FOR INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO REGISTER. Phase-One proposals will be due no earlier than 30 days after the solicitation is released. The exact date and time will be specified in the Phase One solicitation. Proposals must be submitted electronically via PIEE.

title: The Post-wide Construction Multiple Award Task Contract (MATOC)
description: The Army Contracting Command/Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC APG), on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW), seeks Contractor support for The Post-wide Construction Multiple Award Task Contract (MATOC). The requirement will be acquired on an 8(a) small business set-aside competitive basis. Award will be made using the tradeoff method in accordance with FAR Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 15.103-1, by evaluating proposals for the best value that is determined to be the most beneficial to the Government. The first Task Order will be made to execute the seed project under CLIN 0002. The seed project CLIN will identify the tasks required to satisfy fulfillment the requirement. The evaluation methodology for this procurement consists of three (3) factors: Technical, Cost/Price, and Past Performance. Performance Locations include: APG North (Aberdeen), APG South (Edgewood), Adelphi Laboratory Center, Van Bibber Water Treatment Center, Hanson Reservoir, Graces Quarters (Baltimore County), Carroll Island (Baltimore County), Churchville Test Course, Blossom Point Research Facility (Charles County), Adelphi Laboratory Center (Montgomery County) and other areas located in Harford and Baltimore Counties in Maryland. The Contractor shall perform all tasks and services necessary to execute APGs Post Construction MATOC. Contractor must be located within 40 miles of Aberdeen Proving Ground. Award is contingent upon the availability of appropriated funds. The Government reserves the right to cancel this requirement at any time without obligation or liability for proposal preparation costs. The primary North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this solicitation is 236220- Commercial and Institutional Building Construction) the small business size standard is $45 million.

description: BLM-NM RFO COMANCHE OXBOW FENCING This solicitation is being amended to reopened to change the set aside to 100% Total Small Business due to original set-aside resulting in no responses, post it to open market (SAM.gov), update terms and conditions, adding attachments and extend the due date. All questions are due by September 2, 2026 1200 MD. This is a solicitation announcement for fence installation located at the Bureau of Land Management RFO COMANCHE OXBOW, Chaves County, New Mexico near Roswell, NM. 1.1 PROJECT DESCRIPTION Provide all labor, equipment, and materials to remove existing fence and construct approximately 1.2 miles of four strand barbed wire fence according to all Specifications, Drawings, Maps, and Work Data Sheets. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.5 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.7 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.8 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.8.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.8.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. The installation site shall be cleaned up to remove any trash or debris generated by the installation. The unit to be installed is a Steris Power Pack Electric Steam Generator, Part # CH13861. It shall be installed in the same location replacing the old unit and utilizing the same water, power, and discharge lines that are currently in place. The current system in the National Science Laboratories � Gastonia includes 2 Steris steam generators (one not working) and 4 Steris autoclaves. title: Bridge Part Task Trainer (BPTT) Port Databases
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD), Orlando, Florida, intends to award a sole-source contract to General Dynamics Mission Systems (GDMS), CAGE Code 3CX85, Pittsfield, Massachusetts, for the Bridge Part Task Trainer (BPTT) Port Databases. The intended award is authorized under 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. GDMS is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the BPTT Port Databases installed within the Virtual Ship (VShip) system supporting the Royal Saudi Naval Forces (RSNF) Multi-Mission Surface Combatant (MMSC) training system located in Jacksonville, Florida. GDMS is also the sole provider of the VShip licenses used across all BPTTs and possesses the specialized technical expertise required to integrate VShip with the updated operating systems and tactical-system equipment. The requirement includes procuring, delivering, testing, and correcting identified deficiencies associated with export-control-compliant VShip harbor databases and their corresponding electronic charts. These databases will support the RSNF MMSC training system located in Jacksonville, Florida. To comply with Class Determination 2026-O0017, Revision 2, pursuant to RFO Part 6 and DFARS PGI 206.103-170, the Government is seeking information regarding the availability of potential sources capable of providing comparable BPTT Port Databases and associated services. Responses to this Sources Sought notice will be used to determine whether a comparable source is available that could satisfy the Government�s requirements and provide a more advantageous solution. DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The Virtual Ship (VShip) software provides the simulation environment for the BPTT, which includes the U.S. Navy VShip harbor and entity baseline. This software is used to simulate various ship bridge components and scenarios, providing a comprehensive training tool for ship handling, navigation, and overall bridge operations. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: Procure, deliver, test, and correct any identified deficiencies associated with the following export-control-compliant Virtual Ship (VShip) harbors and corresponding electronic charts, ensuring they meet the performance requirements for the current MMSC BPTT Port Databases: Jubayl [ID4.1][QN4.2](Customer's homeport. Including expanded visuals to King Abdulaziz Naval Base) Gibraltar Gulf of Aden Rota Souda Bay Naples Jizan Dammam Jebal Ali Abu Dhabi Bahrain Djibouti Doha Muscat Port Everglades Port Canaveral Key West Salalah Fujairah Yokosuka IVO Oshima Strait (Includes a visual recreation of the USS Fitzgerald collision case study) DELIVERY LOCATIONS: Multi-Mission Surface Combatant (MMSC) 11660 Central Parkway Jacksonville, FL 32228 ELIGIBILITY: North American Industry Classification System - The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services), with an associated small business size standard of 1,250 employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 6910 (Training Aids). SUBMISSION DETAILS: This sources sought notice is not a request for competitive proposals. It is a notice to determine if a comparable source exists and outlines the Government�s intent to contract on a sole source basis with GDMS. REQUIREMENTS Contact the contracting officer listed on page one block 5 of the contract for the "Property of XXXX" on the name plate. 3.1 Reference to Cadmium plating shall be deleted and the following substituted: "Finish shall be electrodeposited alkaline Zinc-Nickel Alloy in accordance with ASTM B 841 Class 1, Type B, Grade 3." 3.2 At faying surfaces, discontinuous welds, or other areas where atmospheric liquids may be retained by capillary action, the crevice shall be sealed using Sealing Compound MIL-S-81733 or equivalent. All containers must be affixed with a nameplate that includes a Unique Identification (UID) marking as referenced in the drawing package Drawing ;(80132) 15930; and IAW Mil-STD-130 latest revision. The contractor shall contact NAVICP code ;N241.17; or code 0771.10 for the alphanumeric sequential serial number group that makes up part of the UID. The UIDwill be included on the nameplate in data matrix format. 3.3 Welding and welder qualifications shall be in accordance with AWS D1.1 for steel, AWS D1.2 or MIL-W-22248,Class 4 for aluminum, AWS D1.3 for sheet steel and AWS D1.6 for stainless steel. Proper controls shall be used to prevent melt through or burn through. For aluminum, filler for welding 6061 alloy shall be 4043: filler for welding 5000 series alloys to themselves or to 6061 shall be 5356 or 5556. In addition,welding and weld inspection shall include: (1) Visual inspection shall include 5X (5power) magnification when a suspect condition is to be examined beyond the capability of normal vision. (2) Critical and major welds may be subjected to further non destructive testing (such as dye penetrant inspection)as prescribed by the buying activity. (3) Proper documentation shall be available for review by Government personnel. 3.4 WORK INSTRUCTIONS. Work instructions shall be posted at theoperator's work station giving procedures to control the welding process, i.e., filler material, weld size, electrical and gas characteristics, including flow rate. 3.5 MATERIALS AND MATERIALS CONTROL. The quality program shall assure that the materials used in fabrication or processing, i.e., base metals and weld filler material, be inspected and conform to the applicable physical, chemical and other technical requirements (supplier's certification is sufficient). 3.6 CONTROLS. Weld filler materials shall be clearly identified and segregated from each other both when in storage and at the work station. Work station environment shall be controlled to prevent conditions adverse to proper gas shielding. 3.7 CLEANING. Parts to be welded shall be cleaned to remove surface soils such as oils, waxes, grease, inks, etc. except that uninhibited alkaline solutions such as sodium hydroxide shall NOT be used. 3.8 DEOXIDIZING. The cleaned parts shall be chemically deoxidized NO MORE THAN 10 DAYS PRIOR TO WELDING to remove thick surface oxide films. (If the material or work is exposed to an outdoor environment, this time limit shall be reduced to a maximum of 3 days, to account for atmospheric effects.) Mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied just prior to the actual start of welding, to remove any reoxidation or residual thin oxide films. 3.8.1 CHEMICAL TREATMENT. An acid deoxidizing treatment shall be applied by either immersion or brushing/wiping. Deoxidizers acceptable for use shall include nitric acid, sulfuric chromic, phosphoric chromic, or equivalent solutions. Sodium hydroxide solutions shall not be used. Care shall be taken to assure 100% solution coverage of the area to be welded. To allow an adequately sized deoxidized area for good welding, the solution shall be applied to an area extending at least 2 inches from the weld site, or ending at any closer adjacent edge. 3.8.2 MECHANICAL MEANS. Immediately prior to welding, mechanical cleaning methods shall be applied to the weld areas previously chemically treated to assure removal of residual or reformed oxides, if any. Acceptable methods of mechanical cleaning include stainless steel wire brushing, scraping, filing, or sanding. However, abrasives containing iron and its oxides, steel wool and wire, and copper alloy based wire, which may become embedded with galvanically active metals and accelerate corrosion of aluminum alloys shall NOT be used. Mechanical methods shall be vigorous enough to adequately remove any residual oxide films, but gentle enough to avoid forming an excessively rough surface in the comparatively soft metal underneath

description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for a commercial product prepared in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12 and RFO Subpart 5.2. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested.This requirement incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01. Requirement Description The U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest, Wind River Ranger District, requires the procurement of a brand new, commercial-grade Fire Trailer Tank and Pump Assembly. Critical Procurement Constraint: The Government currently owns the tandem-axle utility trailer (5�x10�, 7,000 lbs GVWR). This requirement is strictly for the fully integrated skid unit that bolts onto the existing frame. Exclusions: This acquisition explicitly does not include the purchase of a new trailer chassis, wheels, axles, tongue, or towing coupler. Technical Specifications & Salient Characteristics The skid unit must conform to the following core baselines: Tank Structure: Minimum 500-gallon capacity; heavy-duty 10-gauge carbon steel. Internal anti-surge baffles and interior epoxy coating required. Footprint & Weight: Maximum 5�x10� footprint matching the structural channel layout of the government owned trailer. Total assembly dry weight must not exceed 2,300 lbs. Pump Assembly: 13 HP commercial gas engine paired with a twin-impeller portable centrifugal pump delivering ? 120 GPM @ 40 PSI and ? 20 GPM @ 146 PSI. Drafting & Plumbing: Integrated 2-inch manifold with self-loading/drafting system. Includes 2" x 20' suction hose with foot valve/strainer and a manual hand primer pump. Discharges: 2-inch quarter-turn ball valve main discharge. Valved auxiliary ports in 1-inch, 1.5-inch, and 3/4-inch configurations. Accessories: Manual-wind hose reel loaded with 250 feet of 1-inch utility hose and adjustable nozzle. Integrated lockable rear toolbox, shackle tie-down points, and integrated fenders/mud flaps matching tandem-axle placement. Aesthetics: Tank may be painted red but must not feature any fire use decals or markings. ******See Attached Solictation for Salient Characterisitcs******** Place of Performance/ Timelines Delivery/Production Timeline: Full manufacturing, plumbing, leak pressure testing, and final inspection availability must occur within thirty (30) calendar days from receipt of order (ARO). FOB Delivery Address: Wind River Work Center, 1262 Hemlock Road, Carson, WA 98610. Government Pickup Option: If the contractor�s manufacturing facility sits within a 100-mile driving radius of Carson, WA (98610), the Government reserves the right to execute a local pickup. Evaluation Framework & Basis for Award Award will be made to the responsible offeror representing the most advantageous solution to the Government under the simplified procedures of FAR 12.203. The following factors will be evaluated: Technical Acceptability: Exact matching of technical baselines or validated technical justifications for proposed "or equal" elements. Delivery Timeline: Confirmed ability to meet the mandatory 30-day target. Price: Fair and reasonable evaluation. Submission Protocol Quoters must maintain an Active SAM.gov Registration. Offers omitting a Unique Entity ID (UEI) will be immediately excluded from evaluation. Prices must remain firm for 90 calendar days from the submission deadline. Required Package Components: Completed and signed SF-1449 (Blocks 17a, 30a, 30b, and 30c). Phone, Email, and SAM UEI within Block 17a. Completed unit costs and totals within the Schedule of Items. Completed Requirements Compliance Checklist (attached to Solicitation). Technical drawings, dimensional prints, or commercial component brochures. Signed copies of all issued SF-30 Amendments. description: Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC), Crane Division, intends to award the first Job Order (JO) under the sole source Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0016426GMP02. The BOA will be issued to The Boeing Company (Boeing), 460 Herndon PKWY, Herndon, VA 20170-5278. Acquisitions under the BOA will be conducted on a sole source basis in accordance with the statutory 10 U.S.C. 3204 (a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.301-1). The basis for restricting competition is that the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Boeing, is the only one that possesses required skills, software documentation, test fixtures and stations, quality and performance acceptance test procedures experience, and technical data necessary to directly manufacture and produce the hardware wall subscription and licenses needed under this action. Additional bases were unacceptable delays in fulfilling agency requirements through any other source, and duplicative costs to the Government that are not expected to be recovered through competition. The JO is in support of PMA-290 Maritime Patrol and Reconnaissance Aircraft (MPRA) Anti-Surface Warfare Signal Intelligence (ASW SIGINT) for the procurement of assemblies with hard drives and licenses. title: Bottle Field Assessment
description: 3 Sep 26 - Quote due date extended to 8 Sep 26. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for a commercial service prepared in accordance with the format in the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) subpart 12.202, as supplemented with additional information. The Government reserves the right to reject any or all offers received in response to this solicitation. Furthermore, the Government maintains the right to not make an award under this solicitation, and reserves the unilateral right to cancel this solicitation, in whole or in part, at any point prior to award if it is determined to be in the Government's best interest. All solicitation provisions and contract clauses applicable to this procurement are incorporated and set forth in Attachment 2 � SF 1449. Submission of a quote constitutes acknowledgement and acceptance of all terms contained within this attachment. The Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC) Hypervelocity Wind Tunnel 9 in White Oak, Maryland, requires a comprehensive Engineering Assessment of nineteen (19) high-pressure gaseous nitrogen (GN2) storage vessels, collectively known as the "Bottle Field." The objective is to determine the optimal and continued safe operating condition of the facility. The contractor shall perform a multi-phased assessment (Parts I through V) encompassing data collection, Non-Destructive Examination (NDE) plan development and on-site execution, Finite Element Analysis (FEA), and a Minimum Design Metal Temperature (MDMT) evaluation. All engineering analysis must be conducted in strict accordance with API 579 / ASME FFS-1 standards for pressure vessels operating at or above 10,000 psig. See Attachment 1 - Statement of Work (SOW) for full details.

title: Design Build and Design Bid Build Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity Multiple Award Construction Contract for Naval Air Station (NAS) Jacksonville, FL and Naval Station (NS) Mayport, FL
description: The Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Southeast (NAVFAC SE) has been tasked to develop, solicit and award a competitively negotiated Design-Build (DB) and Design-Bid-Build (DBB) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) for new construction, renovation, alteration and repair for general construction projects located at NAS Jacksonville, FL, NS Mayport, FL, and in other locations in the area of operations of NAVFAC SE if deemed necessary and approved by the NAVFAC SE Chief of Contracting Office. A Sources Sought Notice for this requirement was posted on SAM.gov under solicitation N69450-25-R-JMMC on August 26, 2025, requesting small business industry interest and capability statements. Based upon responses from the Notice, the Government concluded that there was enough evaluated small businesses that could meet the minimum requirements and qualifications. Accordingly, the Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued as a competitive small business set aside. All responsible small businesses with the specialized experience and qualifications required by the RFP may submit a proposal to be considered by the Agency. The NAICS code for this IDIQ MACC solicitation is 236220, with a size standard of $45,000,000 ($45M). The Government intends to award approximately five (5) contracts resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offerors whose proposals represent the best value after evaluation in accordance with the factors and their relative importance in the solicitation. Each MACC will have a duration period of one (1) base year and four (4) consecutive option years, totaling five (5) years or an aggregate maximum not-to-exceed (NTE) amount of $249,000,000 ($249M) for all contracts, whichever comes first. Task orders will be firm-fixed-priced, with a minimum value of $350,000 and a maximum value of $10,000,000 ($10M); however, task orders under or over these amounts may be considered if deemed to be in the Government�s best interest and approved by the NAVFAC SE Chief of Contracting Office. Construction projects are planned to be issued as task orders under the MACCs. The work to be performed consists of general building-type projects (new construction, renovation, and demolition) including but not limited to: aviation and aircraft facilities; warehouse, supply, and other industrial facilities; barracks, dormitories, and personnel housing facilities; administrative facilities; training facilities; personnel support and service facilities; maintenance facilities; research facilities; commissaries and retail; medical facilities; waterfront facilities; and other similar types of facilities for NAS Jacksonville, FL and NS Mayport, FL. Projects may require either single discipline or multi-discipline (more than 3 major design disciplines) design services or may include 100% construction performance specifications. Projects may be based on design-build or full plans and specifications delivery method and may also require comprehensive interior design and incorporation of sustainable features. The source selection method to be used is a best value continuum process in a negotiated, two-phase acquisition utilizing the trade-off approach. Formal two-phase source selection will be used to select the proposals that provide the best value to the Government from a technical and price standpoint. In accordance with FAR Subparts 15.1 and 15.2, a trade-off approach to source selection will be used for this solicitation with respect to the initial award. Offerors selected to proceed to Phase Two will be required to submit technical and price proposals for a seed project task order, which will be identified prior to entering into Phase Two. Offerors who fail to submit technical and price proposals will not be considered for an award. The offeror with the best value proposal for the seed project will be awarded an IDIQ contract under the MACC and the seed project task order, subject to funding availability. The remaining selected offerors will be awarded an IDIQ contract under the MACC and a minimum guarantee task order of $1,000.00. This will be an electronic solicitation, which will be posted to Contract Opportunities on the SAM.gov website via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. The solicitation will be available no earlier than 15 days after this pre-solicitation notice is posted. A Pre-Proposal Conference and Site Visit will be held for those offerors chosen to participate in Phase Two, with the exact date and time specified in the Phase Two solicitation. Offerors are responsible for checking the SAM.gov website for the solicitation and any subsequent amendments that may be issued. NO CONTRACT AWARD WILL BE MADE TO ANY CONTRACTOR THAT IS NOT REGISTERED OR IN THE PROCESS OF REGISTERING WITH THE SYSTEM FOR AWARD MANAGEMENT (SAM). PLEASE VISIT THE SAM WEBSITE AT https://www.sam.gov FOR INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO REGISTER. Phase-One proposals will be due no earlier than 30 days after the solicitation is released. The exact date and time will be specified in the Phase One solicitation. Proposals must be submitted electronically via PIEE.

description: RFI Solicitation: RFI #: SPE605-26-RFI-1019 Date Posted: August 26th. 2026 Date Responses Due: September 8th, 2026 This Source Sought Notice (SS) SPE605-26-RFI-1019 is for information and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) - Energy. The purpose of this SS is to identify qualified Businesses that are interested and capable of providing JP8. This SS is issued for a requirement for a DLA-Energy customer located in Tinian, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CMNI). The expected period of performance is December 1, 2026 � January 30, 2027. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. General information regarding RFIs: In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI is issued solely for gathering information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation for proposals. Any response to this notice will be treated as information only. DLA Energy will not provide reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to this RFI. Respondents are advised that DLA Energy is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted under this RFI. Responses to this RFI do not bind DLA Energy to any further actions. Delivery Address: Tinian International Airport Scope: Product Code: JP8 NSN: 9130-01-031-5816 Product Name: TURBINE FUEL, AVIATION Estimated Quantity: 900,000 U.S. Gallons Transport Mode: Barge (BRG) Tank Type 1 and Capacity : Above Ground Tank, 400,000 USG Tank Type 2 and Capacity: Above Ground Tank, 500,000 USG Additional Notes: Tinian Harbor has a shallow draft of 25 feet. Shoaling areas southeast of the northern berthing area have sounding of 17 and 20 feet. Current mudline elevations at Tinian Wharf are approximately 26 feet MLLW within Tinian Harbor, and approximately 28 feet MLLW at the Channel. NOTE: These numbers were measured prior to the Apr 2026 Typhoon Sinlaku. The vendor will be required to make two deliveries: (1) 400,000 USG of JP8 in mid-Dec. 2026, and (2) 500,000 USG of JP8 in mid-Jan. 2027. The vendor is responsible for providing floating booms, boats, and other necessary equipment needed to contain spills during barge delivery. For mid-Dec. delivery, the barge/tanker is required to be in port for APPROXIMATELY FIVE (5) DAYS due to commissioning activities. Assuming the system is fully operations, the rate of fueling for 400,000 USG at 1,000 gpm receipt rate = 400 minutes (or 6.67 hours) plus time to connect/disconnect. For mid-Jan. delivery, the barge/tanker is required to be in port APPROXIMATELY THREE (3) DAYS for initial filling of the second cut and cover tank, pig runs 7-9, and for transferring the remainder of fuel. This will be faster than the mid-Dec. delivery, but it will not be a continuous offloading. For purpose of compiling responses to this Source Sought Notice, the deadline is set on September 8th, 2026, 3:00PM, Fort Belvoir, Virginia Time. In responding to this notice please provide the following information: Your company name, CAGE Code, any owners, email address, and phone numbers. Background information of the firm and/or contractor regarding technical capability and ability to perform. Are you capable of supplying fuel via barge or tanker to Tinian International Airport? Are you able to supply JP8 to Tinian International Airport? What are the names and locations of your fuel supplier(s)? Are you a refinery? Has your company participated in any current or previous contracts under the Direct Delivery Ground Fuels Program? If so, were any of those contracts performed in Guam, Palau, Tinian, or surrounding areas? Remember to Include �RFI# SPE605-26-RFI-1019 Tinian Fuel Commissioning� in the subject line. Responses and/or questions are to be sent to the contracting office points of contact: Katie Richardson at Mary.K.Richardson@dla.mil, Omar Joyce at Omar.Joyce@dla.mil, and DLA Energy FEPAA at DLAENERGYFEPAA@dla.mil. In addition, please ensure the information in the System for Award Management (SAM) website identifies your company status under NAICS 324110. The solicitation will be uploaded to SAM.gov.

title: Prado Dam Spillway Hydroforecasting Services
description: The purpose of this work is to provide streamflow forecasts across short-term (10-day), seasonal (90-day), and annual (daily, 1-year) horizons to enable informed risk-informed decision making. This streamflow model / forecast should contain forecast points at the inflow to Prado Dam, inclusion of historical reforecasts for validation period delivered in CSV files, extended quantiles to enable prescription of the full hydrograph at each model timestep, and clear probabilistic confidence intervals for each forecast point. The model should provide AI powered hydrological and meteorological forecasts in conjunction with traditional models. The AI-powered platform will be expected to deliver precise, multi-horizon streamflow forecasts, from hourly to annual, leveraging deep hydrologic expertise. Its core value lies in accurately predicting rainfall events and basin inflow volumes that could necessitate emergency protective measures within our construction project�s action plan, which mitigates risks to personnel and infrastructure.

The Postal Service bases contract award decisions on best value. The Postal Service is more concerned with making an award at the lowest overall price than with obtaining superior technical or management features. However, the Postal Service may not necessarily make an award at the lowest price to achieve small price savings if better value can be achieved with superior technical or management features. The benefits of a higher priced proposal may merit a higher price. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: The Requirements below will be evaluated on a Pass/Fail Basis. title: Sources Sought Notice SPE605-26-RFI-1019 PC&S 1.8R Tinian
description: RFI Solicitation: RFI #: SPE605-26-RFI-1019 Date Posted: August 26th. 2026 Date Responses Due: September 8th, 2026 This Source Sought Notice (SS) SPE605-26-RFI-1019 is for information and planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) - Energy. The purpose of this SS is to identify qualified Businesses that are interested and capable of providing for the ground fuel requirements for DLA-Energy. This SS is issued for a requirement for a DLA-Energy customer located in Tinian, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CMNI). The expected period of performance is December 1, 2026 � January 30, 2027. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. General information regarding RFIs: In accordance with FAR 15.101(c), responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. This RFI is issued solely for gathering information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation for proposals. Any response to this notice will be treated as information only. DLA Energy will not provide reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to this RFI. Respondents are advised that DLA Energy is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted under this RFI. Responses to this RFI do not bind DLA Energy to any further actions. Delivery Address: Tinian International Airport Scope: Product Code: JP8 NSN: 9130-01-031-5816 Product Name: TURBINE FUEL, AVIATION Estimated Quantity: 900,000 U.S. Gallons Transport Mode: Barge (BRG) Tank Type 1 and Capacity : Above Ground Tank, 400,000 USG Tank Type 2 and Capacity: Above Ground Tank, 500,000 USG Additional Notes: Tinian Harbor has a shallow draft of 25 feet. Shoaling areas southeast of the northern berthing area have sounding of 17 and 20 feet. Current mudline elevations at Tinian Wharf are approximately 26 feet MLLW within Tinian Harbor, and approximately 28 feet MLLW at the Channel. NOTE: These numbers were measured prior to the Apr 2026 Typhoon Sinlaku. The vendor will be required to make two deliveries: (1) 400,000 USG of JP8 in mid-Dec. 2026, and (2) 500,000 USG of JP8 in mid-Jan. 2027. The vendor is responsible for providing floating booms, boats, and other necessary equipment needed to contain spills during barge delivery. For mid-Dec. delivery, the barge/tanker is required to be in port for APPROXIMATELY FIVE (5) DAYS due to commissioning activities. Assuming the system is fully operations, the rate of fueling for 400,000 USG at 1,000 gpm receipt rate = 400 minutes (or 6.67 hours) plus time to connect/disconnect. For mid-Jan. delivery, the barge/tanker is required to be in port APPROXIMATELY THREE (3) DAYS for initial filling of the second cut and cover tank, pig runs 7-9, and for transferring the remainder of fuel. This will be faster than the mid-Dec. delivery, but it will not be a continuous offloading. For purpose of compiling responses to this Source Sought Notice, the deadline is set on September 8th, 2026, 3:00PM, Fort Belvoir, Virginia Time. In responding to this notice please provide the following information: Your company name, CAGE Code, any owners, email address, and phone numbers. Background information of the firm and/or contractor regarding technical capability and ability to perform. Are you capable of supplying fuel via barge or tanker to Tinian International Airport? Are you able to supply JP8 to Tinian International Airport? What are the names and locations of your fuel supplier(s)? Are you a refinery? Has your company participated in any current or previous contracts under the Direct Delivery Ground Fuels Program? If so, were any of those contracts performed in Guam, Palau, Tinian, or surrounding areas? Remember to Include �RFI# SPE605-26-RFI-1019 Tinian Fuel Commissioning� in the subject line. Responses and/or questions are to be sent to the contracting office points of contact: Katie Richardson at Mary.K.Richardson@dla.mil, Omar Joyce at Omar.Joyce@dla.mil, and DLA Energy FEPAA at DLAENERGYFEPAA@dla.mil. In addition, please ensure the information in the System for Award Management (SAM) website identifies your company status under NAICS 324110. The solicitation will be uploaded to SAM.gov.

description: Solicitation for Air Force Civil Engineer Center (AFCEC) Operation Support Services Tyndall AFB, FL. This is an announcement for a competitive total small business 8(a) set-aside for a service acquisition as required by the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 5. This is a Request for Proposal (RFP). Vendors shall submit proposals in response to this announcement. The purpose of this contract is to provide operation support services for AFCEC at Tyndall AFB, FL in accordance with the Performance Work Statement (PWS) in a manner that supports all phases of the civil engineer research, development, and acquisition process. The contractor shall provide management and labor support necessary to provide baseline operations support capability for AFCEC, including crosscutting operational functions; maintenance of facilities at TAFB FL and aid (e.g., produce prototypes, test articles etc. as described in PWS para 1.2) in accomplishing Research Development Test and Evaluation (RDTE), Airforce Pavement Evaluation (APE) Team and other projects and events on TAFB, FL. This includes maintaining the AFCEC Readiness Directorate, Requirements and Acquisition Division (AFCEC/CXA) test ranges and facilities (i.e., Bldg. 1117, facilities in the 9700 area, AFCEC fire research area at Silver Flag, test ranges, and other facilities managed by AFCEC at Tyndall Air Force Base (TAFB), FL; to include occupants assigned to these facilities by AFCEC and/or aiding organizations with AFCEC support agreements. All work performed by the contractor shall be performed in accordance with all applicable laws, regulations, Air Force (AF) standards and policies, instructions, and commercial practices. The duration of this contract is expected to be for a base period of twelve months plus four option years at twelve months each. The solicitation will be for a commercial service and prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12 Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The solicitation will result in a firm, fixed price contract. The successful contractor will be selected using Best Value Trade-Off source selection procedures, resulting in the best value for the Government. description: The Facilities Construction R&A East CMT of the United States Postal Service is soliciting proposals for a Pavement & Retaining Wall Repair project, at the United States Postal Service owned Ciales MPO 25 Carrera 149, Ciales, PR 00638-9998, Arecibo County. Please see attached Summary of Work. The estimated cost of the work is between $2,000,000 and $3,000,000; with construction completion no later than three hundred sixty-five (365) calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed. The solicitation will open August 7, 2026 on USPS eSourcing Coupa (see How to Participate below) and close on September 8, 2026. A pre-proposal meeting for this project will be held on August 17, 2026 at 10:00am, (local time) on site. Attendance is not mandatory but is strongly recommended. Technical inquiries are to be addressed to Victor Morales, Architect/Engineer, AECOM Caribe LLP, at (787) 516-3770, or the USPS Project Manager, Miguel Casiano at (787) 622-1807. The Postal Service bases contract award decisions on best value. The Postal Service is more concerned with making an award at the lowest overall price than with obtaining superior technical or management features. However, the Postal Service may not necessarily make an award at the lowest price to achieve small price savings if better value can be achieved with superior technical or management features. The benefits of a higher priced proposal may merit a higher price. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: The Requirements below will be evaluated on a Pass/Fail Basis. Experience Profile: Two examples of comparable projects as defined on form under Attachment 22: Experience Profile. Years in Business: Proof of having been in the construction business for a minimum of 5 consecutive years. Price Proposal: Signed Offer and Award (Page 1), Schedule of Values (see eRFX Excel Attachment), Schedule of Unit Prices (if applicable), and Schedule of Alternates (if applicable). Terms & Conditions: Affirmation of Contract Terms, Acknowledgement of Solicitation Amendments; (if applicable), Provision F-202: Key Personnel; Provision 4-3: Representations and Certifications; Provision 1-3: Domestic Source Certificate - Construction Materials; and Provision F-401: Authorized Negotiators. Form VETS-4212 Documentation is required. If you are not registered with Department of Labor Report System, you must register on the DOL website at: https://vets4212.dol.gov/vets4212 and provide proof of registration. Please Note: Bonding: Contractor must have the ability to obtain 100 percent performance and payment bonds for this project in seven (7) calendar days of receipt of a Notice of Intent to Award. All projects are solicited and awarded as singular events. Awardees may have multiple projects in the construction phase at the same time and would be required to obtain full bonding for each project during the agreed upon construction period. Construction will not be delayed due to the inability to acquire and maintain bonding on multiple projects simultaneously. Contractor will be responsible for coordination of all work in a manner that will not interfere with mail operations and coordinate all work related to this phased project with the Facility Manager or designee. Note: Successful offeror will be required to submit a Sub-Contracting Plan and Project Specific Safety Plan acceptable to the USPS Contracting Officer before a Notice to Proceed (NTP) is issued. The successful offeror will be bound by the Contractor's Screening Requirements. Offerors must familiarize themselves with the requirements of Clause F-102. HOW TO PARTICIPATE IN THE OPPORTUNITY All proposals must be submitted online in USPS eSourcing. USPS eSourcing Coupa is a web-based electronic solicitation platform. If your organization wishes to participate in this solicitation and is not registered in Coupa, please see the attached Coupa registration instructions. Complete the form and submit to the email on the form. Once the registration process is complete, the Postal Service will review the entry within seven (7) business days to ensure it is complete and accurate. Upon approval, you will be notified via e-mail of your log-in credentials. Once you receive confirmation your account is active, reach out to the Point of Contact and request an invitation to the event. If you have any questions on the registration process, refer to the attached PowerPoint presentations to aid in registering and managing the event. If your company is already registered in Coupa, contact Jennifer Santiago at Jennifer.Santiago@usps.gov or (860) 285-7138 to request an invitation to bid. Separate electronic messages will be sent inviting you to participate in the solicitation and notifying you when the event is opened. Each organization must "accept" the Invitation to place a bid in Coupa. Any required documentation may be attached to your bid after submitting total dollar amount of bid in Coupa. CLOSING TIME WILL NOT BE EXTENDED DUE TO OPERATOR INABILITY WITHIN COUPA.
