title: Z2DA--589A4-25-102, Install Dedicated Pharmacy Air Handler
description: THIS IS A PRESOLICITATION NOTICE ONLY PRESOLICITATION NOTICE- Install Dedicated Pharmacy Air Handler Project Number 589A4-25-102 Scope of work: The Harry S Truman Veterns Memorial Hospital in Columbia, MO requires the installation of three dedicated air handling units (AHUs) to bring the pharmacy and compounding, located in building one, in compliance with the latest VA HVAC Design Manual. The air handlers will serve the compounding area on the third floor, and the pharmacy and compounding areas in the basement. The project design includes a new dedicated DOAS located in E002B in the Basement to serve the Compounding Suite in the Basement. There will be two new dedicated Air Handling Units in a new Mechanical space in the Southeast corner of the Second Floor Roof. Construction Phasing Installation of the new mechanical equipment will precede the demolition of the existing units. Temporary units will be provided for service while the first existing Mechanical units is demolished and removed. The same procedure will occur for the remainder of the Mechanical units. Selective Mechanical Demolition The main supply and return trunks serving the pharmacy and compounding areas in the basement will be demolished back to the plenum. The plenum will be patched and repaired. All but one VAV terminal units will remain in place. One VAV will be removed and prepared for relocation. The supply trunk supplying the compounding areas on the third floor will be partially demolished back to the last VAV on the trunk. Also, the supply trunk supplying the air flow control valves will require a partial demolition. Proposed Mechanical System Description There will be a new dedicated DOAS located in room E002B in the basement to serve the compounding suite in the basement. This AHU will be 4000 cfm with a chilled water cooling coil, steam heating coil, duct mounted humidifier, supply fan, two duct mounted pre-filters, a duct mounted after filter, and a duct mounted HEPA filter rack for emergency mode. Campus chilled water will be utilized for the cooling coil. The existing low-pressure steam (12 psi) system will be used for the pre-heat coil. Direct digital controls (DDC) controls will be installed and integrated into the BMS for monitoring and remote control of the DOAS. The exhaust system will remain in place and be interlocked with the AHU via DDC controls. There will be two AHUs installed in a new penthouse located on the second-floor roof in the southeast corner. Both AHUs will utilize the campus chilled water and heating hot water. Chilled water and heating hot water will be routed from the basement to the new penthouse and connected to duplex hot water pumps and duplex chilled water pumps. The pumps will operate one on, one standby and provide redundancy. The AHU to serve the compounding on third floor will be a DOAS. The DOAS will be 2500 cfm with a chilled water coil, hot water coil, humidifier section, supply fan, two pre-filters, an after filter, and a HEPA filter rack for emergency epidemic mode. The supply duct will be routed into the interstitial space between the second-floor roof and third-floor. The duct will be continue through the interstitial space to the north side of the building and rise up into the third-floor ceiling to connect to three existing airflow control valves. The AHU to serve the pharmacy areas on the first-floor and basement will also be located in the new penthouse. The AHU will be approximately 4500 cfm with a chilled water coil, hot water coil, humidifier, supply fan, return fan, two pre-filters and an after filter and a HEPA filter. The supply and return duct will turn down into the second-floor ceiling in the penthouse. The duct will be routed down a new chase into the ceiling of the first-floor. Once in the first-floor ceiling new branch ducts will take off to connect to the first-floor pharmacy terminal units and return grilles. The main ducts will continue down a new chase into the basement pharmacy ceiling. A new supply and return trunk will be routed down the center of the pharmacy area and new branch ducts will connect to existing terminal units and return grilles. All new equipment installed will be complete with DDC controls and integrated into the BMS for monitoring and remote control. The Estimated range to complete this work is $2,000,000.00 to $5,000,000.00. Pursuant to 38 USC 8127(d) and in accordance with Public Law 109-461, the Veterans Benefits, Health Care and Information Technology Act of 2006, this construction project will be solicited as a Total set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS) for this procurement is 236220 (General Construction Contractors), with a small business size standard of $45.0 million. The duration of the project will be 540 calendar days from Notice to Proceed to include contract closeout. This completion period includes submittals, all construction work, final inspection, cleanup of the premises and completion of as-built drawings and close-out documents. Award will be made utilizing the Lowest Price Technical Acceptable (LPTA ) Best Value type. Source Selection Process in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 15. Proposal submission instructions will be included in the solicitation package. The government plans to award without discussions. Offerors are responsible to monitor and download all Solicitation documents, Specifications, Drawings from the Sam contract opportunities website: https://sam.gov/content/opportunities and any amendments that may be issued for this solicitation. In accordance with FAR 52.204-7, Required SAM and in accordance with Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 802.101, SBA Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert) Registration, prospective contractors must be registered in SAM and in the SBA Vetcert databases under the applicable NAICS. Firms may obtain SAM information at https://sam.gov/content/home and SBA VetCert https://veterans.certifysba.gov. The solicitation package and drawings should be available for download on or about August 7, 2026, and the proposal due date will be on or about September 8, 2026. An organized site visit will be scheduled, and the information will be made available at time of solicitation issuance. Only one site visit will be scheduled and interested offerors are highly encouraged to attend. No hard copies of the solicitation or drawings will be provided; and telephone questions will NOT be accepted. title: Digital Magazines - Notice of Intent to Award Sole Source
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD SOLE SOURCE The 772d Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract to a single source, OVERDRIVE, INC., under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b)(2) (only one source reasonably available) on 30 September 2026. The period of performance (PoP) shall be: 30 September 2026 � 29 September 2029. PSC: 7630 NAICS: 516210 Small Business Size Standard: $47M Subscription: Digital Magazine collection Supplier: OVERDRIVE, INC. Product Description: DOD Libraries has a requirement to procure a digital magazines/journals platform subscription that allows for downloadable magazines. Magazines have no circulation cap and allow unlimited simultaneous use so patrons can enjoy every issue of every magazine. With smart tags that ensure library users can be notified when each new issue is released. Must be able to provide a collection of several thousand magazines on an existing commercial off the shelf platform in the library marketplace. Product characteristics an equal item must meet to be considered: Must be able to provide full-color digital magazines on the Overdrive Platform already under contract with DoD Libraries Must be able to be accessed/read on desktops, mobile devices, or apps Magazines must be downloadable on at least 90% of mobile devices including iOS (Apple�), Android�, and Kindle Fire�/HD/HDX Database must contain a collection of popular digital magazines with both new and backlist titles Magazine must be available without holds, checkout periods, no limits and provide full list of magazine titles in the Simultaneous Use Must provide popular titles such as Us Weekly, Good Housekeeping, Vanity Fair, and Rolling Stone Must provide special interest titles such as PC World, Bon Appetit, Minecraft World, and Women�s Fitness Must provide titles in a variety of languages including Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Italian, German, French, and more Must provide a rolling 3 years of back issues, wherever available Must be able to curated and weeded magazines available Must provide marketing resources for DOD Libraries to promote the content to customers Must be able to search and checkout collection by newest issue, keyword search, genre and language Must provide the user a magazine in the collection, they can open it and start reading with one tap, generating a checkout for your library. Must provide a streamlined access to magazines will have a new dedicated section. This will help users find their favorite magazines from the library in one convenient place. Must provide text to speech function Must distribute digitally overseas Must work with a magazine publishers that sells to the Government Access to information needs to be seamless, minimal response time between query initiation and query results, and search results within 5-10 seconds. Must be able to interface with all 4 service branch library single sign on an industry standard authentication method to ensure only eligible patrons can access resources from any internet connected computer browsers and mobile devices. Must work with contract POC to establish authentication methods to provide optimal accessibility for all eligible patrons. Security between the Website and server must be Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 Must be able to supply or allow retrieval of database usage statistics by Branch of Service (Air Force, Army, Marine Corps, Other, and Navy) Must have HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) with long duration deployed on the servers to mitigate/prevent man-in-the-middle attacks Website certificates should be RSA 2048-bits (SHA256withRSA) VCL must be able to test the platform to evaluate if it meets requirements. Must provide username and password to view content on platform.. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the Government. The Government will consider responses received by 8 September 2026, 2:00 PM, CST for this notice. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this announcement. A determination not to compete this requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Contractors Should Be Aware of the Following Information: 1. Contractors MUST include the following information: a. Points of contact, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers. b. Identification as a large U.S. business, a small U.S. business, or a foreign business. Please note that size indicated should be based on the NAICS code for this effort listed above. c. Identification of any other socioeconomic status including Women-Owned Small Business, Economically Disadvantaged Small Business, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Veteran Owned Small Business or HUBZone. d. Company CAGE Code and UEI. 2. If this posting specifically references brand name products, offerors are encouraged to suggest products other than those specifically referenced. Responses must address how the alternate product meets the product characteristics specified above. 3. Submitted information shall be UNCLASSIFIED. 4. Responses are limited to 10 pages in a Microsoft Word or PDF compatible format. Responses shall be e-mailed to Contracting Specialist: SrA William Sasser at william.sasser.2@us.af.mil and Contracting Officer: TSgt Vaughn Swinton at vaughn.swinton@us.af.mil no later than 8 September 2026 at 2:00 PM CST.

title: PN: 636A8-22-001, Reno 6th Floor Clinical Support (IC)
description: The project to consist of approximately 22,500 sq. ft. The goal to provide suitable space for the clinical support staff that serve the inpatient units on the 5th and 7th floors. The support staff to include space for social workers, physicians, nutritionists, education staff. The majority of the renovation will result in offices, conference, storage, and staff workrooms, a clean and soiled utility rooms, reception area, lactation room, electrical closet, and restrooms. The clinical areas include EMG and NVC exam rooms. The existing Sleep Lab and Physical Therapy department currently located on the 6th floor are to remain on the 6th floor. The sleep lab serves a dual patient role of seeing patients mainly in the evening but during the day the sleep rooms are also used for neurological testing serving as Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Velocity (NCV) exams. The sleep lab will have to remain in operation during construction, and a phased schedule is required.

title: Top Wind Tunnels
description: The U.S. Army TMDE Activity (USATA) has a requirement to purchase of two (2) Wind Tunnels that will be used by USATA Engineers and Technicians to provide OCONUS support to customers owning wind speed measuring devices (hot-wire anemometers). Industrial hygiene and chemical testing facilities are impacted by the increased turn-around time of sending their equipment to the APSL. The Wind Tunnels shall include the following specifications or equivalent (if not brand name): Requirements: The wind tunnel shall generate air speeds ranging from 1.5 to 50 m/s. Air speed measuring equipment shall be provided and shall have a total measurement uncertainty less than or equal to 0.75% of reading. The wind tunnel test chamber shall have cross sectional dimensions of 4 x 4 inch at minimum, and 12 x 12 inch at maximum. The wind tunnel shall produce turbulence intensity that is less than or equal to 1%. The wind tunnel shall have maximum dimensions of 10 x 3 x 6 feet LWH when assembled. The wind tunnel shall be able to fit through a standard 32-inch width door. The wind tunnel design shall be open circuit if a closed-circuit design is not available within budget. For designs greater than 45 kg, the wind tunnel shall be built on a frame with casters. The wind tunnel�s motor shall not exceed 90 dB when generating speeds of 50 m/s. The wind tunnel�s motor shall be powered on a 220V 16A single phase line. Support and Accessories The wind tunnel shall be shipped to TMDE Support Center (TSC) Kaiserslautern, Germany and TSC Camp Carroll, South Korea. Measuring equipment requires organic calibration support. Any calibration procedure/software required shall be provided. All software shall not require an annual subscription or online connection. If software does not have a transferable license, a computer shall be provided to operate it. Operating software shall be able to report standard and actual wind speed. It shall also be able to correct for different pressure and temperature conditions. Operating software shall be able to export data from test runs.

description: Notice to Offeror(s)/Supplier(s): Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made under this solicitation until funds are available. The Government reserves the right to cancel this solicitation, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. The Government requests quotes remain firm through September 30, 2026. If market volatility prevents this, clearly state the maximum length of time quote pricing can be held. Pest Management Tractor and Sprayer ProGator 2030A (Diesel) and HD300 SelectSpray (For ProGators 2020A and 2030A) Brand Name or Equal all components must be brand new These can be categorized as follows: 1. Engine: Engine Type: Three-cylinder, liquid-cooled diesel engine. Displacement: 77.3 cu in. Horsepower: 23.9 hp (25.4 kW) at 3600 rpm. Fuel System: Electronic Fuel Injection (EFI). EFI provides efficient fuel delivery, responsive acceleration, excellent fuel economy, and quick starting even in cold weather. Engine Controller: Located under the cargo box and inside the right rear corner of the frame, the engine controller regulates engine speed based on the electronic throttle pedal input. Fuel Tank: Large 30.7 L (8.1 US gal) EPA- and CARB-compliant fuel tank. 2. Drivetrain: Transmission: Kanzaki five-speed synchro-mesh with five forward gears and one reverse gear. Drive System: 2WD is standard, with a manual engage on-demand 4WD option available. Brakes: Four-wheel hydraulic drum brakes. Axles: Rear axles (LH and RH). 3. Electrical System: Alternator: 55 amp, regulated. Battery: 12V, 500 CCA. Ignition: Transistor Controlled Ignition with electric start. Lighting: Halogen headlights. Instrumentation: Hour meter, tachometer, digital speedometer, Power Take-Off (PTO) light, engine coolant temperature gauge, voltage indicator light, 4WD indicator light, oil pressure light, and horn. 4. Frame, Suspension, and Operator Station: Frame: The vehicle is built on a robust frame. Suspension: Dual leaf springs and shock absorbers on both the front and rear. Operator Station: Includes two professional high-back, tilt-forward seats, seat belts, a glove box, and cup holders. ROPS: Two-post Roll-Over Protection Structure (ROPS) is standard, with a four-post conversion kit available. 5. Other Notable Components: Air Cleaner: Replaceable dual dry-type element air cleaner with remote intake. Enclosed Cab: Heater/AC Cargo Box: Optional accessory. Steering: Hydraulic power steering. Attachments: The vehicle can accommodate various attachments, such as auxiliary hydraulics, cargo boxes, and different tire options. Pesticide/Herbicide Attached Sprayer Designed for specific compatible use with purchased Utility Vehicle listed above required to be composed of several key components that work together to provide efficient and versatile spraying capabilities. Here's a breakdown of its generic components: Tank: Impact-resistant polyethylene tank with a 1136 L (300 U.S. gal.) capacity, featuring a low center of gravity and visibility. It includes jet agitation, a quick-fill feature with anti-siphon protection, a sloped sump for draining, a vent line with a check valve, and a removable basket strainer. Pump: Offers a choice between diaphragm or centrifugal pumps. Diaphragm Pump: Suitable for turf paint and higher pressures (up to 20 bar / 290 psi), handling thicker fluids and capable of running dry. Requires a pressure relief valve. Centrifugal Pump: Provides higher flow rates (up to 397 L/min / 105 gpm) at lower pressures (around 6.6 bar / 95 psi). Available in cast iron or stainless steel. Includes an automatic air bleed line. Booms: Heavy-duty construction with adjustable width and height. Available in 18 ft (5.5 m) or 15/21 ft (4.6/6.4 m) widths. Features a bidirectional breakaway and triple-nozzle bodies on 20-inch (50.8 cm) spacing. Includes a standard electro-hydraulic lift system. Control Systems: Options for Manual or Automatic Rate Control. Manual Rate Controller: Pressure-based system with a weather-resistant box and liquid pressure gauge, controlling boom functions and pressure. Automatic Rate Controller: Adjusts application rate based on speed, with a digital display for various parameters and a nozzle display. A common wiring harness allows switching between controllers. Electrical components are housed in a convenient box. Other Standard Features: Includes an electric pressure/flow regulator, a self-cleaning 100-mesh filter, electric boom shutoff valves, and adjustable throttling valves. A personal wash system is standard. A foam marker is optional. Easy Removal and Installation: The sprayer can be easily detached by removing pins, electrical connectors, and hydraulic lines. Optional storage stands are available. Important Notes: The automatic rate controller uses the purchased utility vehicle speed sensor, flow meter, and a digital pressure sensor for accuracy.

description: AMENDMENT NO. 3 SOLICITATION NO. 36C24126Q0652 DATE: 8/28/2026 1. THE SOLICITATION IS HEREBY AMENDED AS FOLLOWS: a. RFI QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS The Amendment No. 1 header identifies Solicitation 36C24126Q0652, while page 3 identifies Solicitation 36C24126Q0601. Please confirm Amendment No. 1 applies to Solicitation 36C24126Q0652. Yes Amendment No. 1 applies to Solicitation 36C24126Q0652. The 0601 header is a clerical typo. Please confirm that the revised Performance Work Statement and Revised Line-Item Template replace the previous versions in their entirety, and that the requirement consists of the following four-line items with no option items: Building 5, Building 60 East, building 60 North, and Building 60 West. Confirmed. Amendment No. 1 explicitly states the attached Revised Performance Work Statement replaces the previous PWS in its entirety and instructs offerors to use the Revised Line-Item Template for pricing. The solicitation instructions require evidence of original equipment manufacturer training or certifications. Please identify the specific manufacturer training or certifications required and confirm whether qualifications held by the proposed installing subcontractor may satisfy this requirement. OEM training/certifications held by your proposed installing subcontractor may satisfy this requirement, so long as the certifications are relevant to the specified door systems/operators and the subcontractor will perform the associated work. The revised Performance Work Statement states that Wel-Design Alarm Systems is the only approved contractor with logical access for integration and testing. Please confirm whether the prime contractor must subcontract with and include Wel-Design s costs in its quote. If so, please provide the current Wel-Design point of contact for this project. There is existing low voltage hardware that is currently functioning, but the PWS will replace attached hardware with a selection made by the prime contractor. Sole source is not specified because the prime contractor could assume the risk and speculate their chosen hardware solution is plug- and play and not require Wel-design services. We would deem this a high risk choice but is the bidders discretion on firm fixed price risk vs reward decision making. Contact - Robert Wood rwood@encorefireprotection.com SEE also https://encorefireprotection.com/affiliated-brand/wel-design-alarm-systems/ Please confirm whether an offeror may use the recent and relevant past performance of a proposed major subcontractor or teaming partner to satisfy the requirement for at least three similar contracts. The RFQ requires at least three recent/relevant contracts of similar scope and does not limit those to the prime contractor only. In line with FAR past performance practices, you may submit past performance for a proposed major subcontractor or teaming partner when that firm will perform critical aspects of the requirement. Please confirm the applicable Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation Limitations on Subcontracting certification and the applicable Federal Acquisition Regulation 52.219-14 performance category for this requirement. The solicitation includes Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation 852.219-76 for supplies and products, while the revised Performance Work Statement describes a turnkey commercial service involving physical door replacement. This was an error and the correct VAAR clause applicable to the solicitation is VAAR 852.219 75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction. Please confirm whether Service Contract Labor Standards Wage Determination No. 2015-6115 is the only wage determination applicable to this requirement or whether a Construction Wage Rate Requirements determination also applies. SCLS WD 2015 6115 Revision 5 is the confirmed applicable wage determination for this solicitation as issued. Construction Wage Rate Requirements do not apply as the solicitation is for commercial services. Please confirm when the 90-calendar-day period begins and whether that period includes product-submittal review, fabrication, procurement lead time, installation, testing, and closeout. 90-days is intended to cover award to installation and closeout. VA review occurs within 7 calendar days for commercial service. Please identify the minimum required warranty periods for doors, frames, glass, operators, hardware, electrical work, Physical Access Control System integration, and installation labor. Typical warranty expectation is 1-year, other clauses like latent defect and negligence notwithstanding. Can the VA please lay out, in a one-line diagram for each door, the access control & door operator components, both new and existing that are to re-purposed, with preferred locations that are to be installed. Not for these areas but a typical 1 line with operator and access control is now attached. (Please see the attachment labeled AccessControlStandardDetail). Please confirm that there are no hazardous materials present. All current testing and knowledge to date does not indicate any abatement required of ACM or lead. Should indications arise the contract scope for that area will be terminated and the VA shall address. Abatement is not permitted under commercial service. Please confirm if the supervisor can act as SSHO and CQC as well. Commercial services solicitations use performance based requirements and rely on general safety and QA clauses (e.g., FAR 52.212 4), not construction specific safety & quality control frameworks. Can the Government formally confirm that this Building 5 doorway is being permanently and officially decommissioned as a designated emergency exit? Specifically, we want to verify that once the signage is replaced and the door is converted to a commercial roll-up cart entrance, this doorway will be classified as a non-exit utility opening, thereby ensuring full code compliance and relieving the contractor of any life-safety liability for the roll-up door installation. (Context: Section 1.2.3.b of the Revised PWS instructs the contractor to "Replace of signage designating the new rollup as an exit. Occupants to be directed to an alternative by replacement signage." Furthermore, Section 1.2.1.6 requires an Interim Life Safety Measure (ILSM) assessment for the "closure of any egress." Under NFPA 101, installing an overhead commercial roll-up door is strictly prohibited along active emergency egress routes.) Confirmed. Not an emergency exit. Amendment 1 states that the revised PWS replaces the previous PWS in its entirety and that all other solicitation terms and conditions remain unchanged. Can the Government please confirm that the Technical Proposal submission requirements identified in the original solicitation under Instructions to Offerors remain applicable, in addition to the Bidding Requirements identified in Section 4 of the revised PWS? Yes, see question 2. Amendment 1 explicitly states that the Revised PWS replaces only the prior PWS, and that all other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged. description: INTRODUCTORY / EXPLANATORY STATEMENT FOR SAM.gov POSTING Attachment: FY26 ETMPM�TENS Procurement Program � Consolidated Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Enterprise Procurement Office (EPO), is posting the attached Consolidated Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) document to SAM.gov to ensure that all interested industry partners, those known to the VA and those unknown receive the exact same information, at the same time, and from the same authoritative source. This approach reflects the VA�s commitment to fairness, openness, and strict adherence to Federal procurement integrity requirements throughout the FY26 Electro?Therapeutic Modalities for Pain Management (ETMPM) � Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulation (TENS) Procurement Program. The attached FAQ consolidates all clarifications generated during market research, RFI interactions, and Vendor engagement activities. No proprietary guidance, unequal insights, or individualized direction will be provided to any prospective Offeror outside officially posted public notices. FAR 15.201(e) strictly limits the type of information the Government may provide during exchanges prior to the release of a solicitation; therefore, this consolidated posting serves as the singular, uniformly accessible communication vehicle for presolicitation clarifications. To preserve the integrity of this competitive procurement, the VA cannot engage in direct, one?off correspondence with individual Vendors regarding acquisition strategy, evaluation criteria, product eligibility, or any other elements that may advantage one party over another. All inquiries must be directed to the EPO AS4D Contracting Officer only through the formal channels specified in future solicitation documents, and any additional clarifications will be issued publicly through SAM.gov where every stakeholder has equal access. The VA has taken extensive measures to ensure transparency, consistency, and broad dissemination of program information. These safeguards include: Consolidating all vendor questions and Government responses into a single, uniform FAQ document. Publishing updates exclusively to SAM.gov to prevent fragmentation or unequal communication. Applying strict correspondence controls that prevent private advisory, selective feedback, or privileged insights. Ensuring that small businesses, including newly established or previously unknown SDVOSB/VOSB firms receive the same updates as long?standing industry partners. Maintaining traceable, public release points so all parties can rely on one authoritative location for official procurement information. By issuing this FAQ as a public attachment, the VA reinforces its long?standing practice of maintaining full procurement integrity, equal?access communications, and industry?wide fairness. The VA appreciates the participation and professionalism of all prospective Offerors and looks forward to continued engagement under the formal solicitation once released.

title: UPGRADE ENTRANCE PORTAL AT BROOHAVEN NATIONAL LABORATORY
description: Brookhaven Science Associates, LLC (BSA), the Management and Operating (M&O) contractor for Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL), intends to construct a new entrance portal at the Laboratory's primary entrance. The existing Main Gate security access point (Building 680), constructed in 1960, has exceeded its useful service life and requires replacement. The project will replace the existing entrance and provide a modernized entrance portal featuring fully integrated security booths to monitor, screen, and process personnel and vehicular traffic entering the Laboratory. The new portal will provide weather protection for security personnel, enhanced site lighting, and a modern traffic control system designed to improve safety, efficiency, and operational reliability. The upgraded entrance will also complement the adjacent, publicly accessible Science and User Support Center (SUSC) by providing a secure, efficient, and welcoming point of entry to the Laboratory. The scope of work for the contract includes the demolition and removal of the existing security booths and associated infrastructure, and the construction of a new entrance portal facility, including structural systems, utilities, security systems, site improvements, and all supporting infrastructure required for full operational capability. BSA will furnish two (2) prefabricated security booths as Government-Furnished Property (GFP). Solicitation documents are available at the link provided in this notice. Pursuant to FAR Part 10 (Market Research), the purpose of this notice is to: (1) Determine if sources capable of satisfying the agency's requirements exists. (2) Determine if commercial items suitable to meet the agency's needs are available or could be modified to meet the agency's requirements. (3) Determine the commercial practices of company's engaged in providing the needed service or supply. Pursuant to FAR Part 6 and FAR Part 19, competition and set-aside decisions may be based on the results of this market research. This notice in no way obligates the Government to any further action. REQUIREMENT: This notice is issued by the U.S. Coast Guard, CG-DCS-SEA-C, Base Alameda, CA to identify sources capable of providing the following: The U.S. Coast Guard is looking for sources which would be interested in performing Dry Dock repairs for the United States Coast Guard Cutter (USCGC) ANVIL (WLIC-75301). The performance period start date of this upcoming Dry Dock is 23 February 2027. title: UPGRADE ENTRANCE PORTAL AT BROOHAVEN NATIONAL LABORATORY
description: Amendment No. 1 (dated 8/17/26) provides responses to vendor questions. Use the shared link provided in this notice to access the contract documents, including all amendments. Brookhaven Science Associates, LLC (BSA), the Management and Operating (M&O) contractor for Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL), intends to construct a new entrance portal at the Laboratory's primary entrance. The existing Main Gate security access point (Building 680), constructed in 1960, has exceeded its useful service life and requires replacement. The project will replace the existing entrance and provide a modernized entrance portal featuring fully integrated security booths to monitor, screen, and process personnel and vehicular traffic entering the Laboratory. The new portal will provide weather protection for security personnel, enhanced site lighting, and a modern traffic control system designed to improve safety, efficiency, and operational reliability. The upgraded entrance will also complement the adjacent, publicly accessible Science and User Support Center (SUSC) by providing a secure, efficient, and welcoming point of entry to the Laboratory. The scope of work for the contract includes the demolition and removal of the existing security booths and associated infrastructure, and the construction of a new entrance portal facility, including structural systems, utilities, security systems, site improvements, and all supporting infrastructure required for full operational capability. BSA will furnish two (2) prefabricated security booths as Government-Furnished Property (GFP). Solicitation documents are available at the link provided in this notice. Mandatory Solicitation Overview Meeting and Site Visit An in-person Solicitation Overview Meeting and Site Visit are MANDATORY for all prospective offerors. Failure to attend both the Solicitation Overview Meeting and the Site Visit will render an offeror ineligible for award under this solicitation. The RSVP must include each attendee's full name and citizenship status. Failure to provide the required information will prevent attendee registration and site access. All attendees must comply with Brookhaven National Laboratory's REAL ID requirements for site access. Additional information is available at: https://www.bnl.gov/real-id/index.php. Questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted via email to jfamiglie@bnl.gov no later than the date and time identified above and in accordance with the instructions contained in the solicitation. description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE In support of Project No: OC-2026-134408 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Office of Acquisitions and Grants Services, Office of the Chief Scientist (OCS) intends to award a firm fixed price purchase order to Milestone, Inc, 25 Controls Drive, Shelton, CT, 06484 for the purchase of the Milestone Total-Care Service Contract, including yearly maintenance in which all valves, hoses, connections, and safety components that are in constant contact with high pressure and high temperature acid vapors are replaced proactively. All other components are thoroughly cleaned, inspected, calibrated, and tested. Batch certification of color additives is a regulatory premarket enforcement function. During the certification process, analyses are performed to determine whether each batch meets the specifications listed in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR). Results are used to certify or reject batches of color additives intended for use in foods, drugs, and cosmetics in the U.S. The microwave digestion equipment is an UltraWAVE3 single reaction chamber (SRC) with serial number 23090033. This is the primary instrument used to prepare color additives for elemental analysis by inductively coupled plasma (ICP) � mass spectrometry (MS) at the Division of Color Certification and Color Technology (DCCT). The digestion process breaks down color additives into a clear, particle-free, and acidic solution. Reliable and timely maintenance and repairs of the microwave digestion system is critical to the mission of the Color Certification Program. The UltraWAVE 3 SRC microwave digestion unit shall be maintained and repaired under the new service agreement and the service agreement shall meet or exceed the requirements/specification listed below. Service and Support: The Contractor shall provide at least one yearly preventive maintenance service. The Contractor shall provide unlimited phone support. The Contractor shall cover all travel, non-consumable parts, and labor for yearly preventive maintenance service at no additional cost to the Government. Written reports shall be provided for all on-site service work within 7 business days of completion. Repairs � Repairs shall be performed on-site at CPK2 (see Section 9, Place of Performance) with parts, labor, and travel costs covered by the Contractor. � Requests for repair visits are unlimited. The Contractor shall provide service and application support within 2 business days and on-site repairs within 7 business days. � Repair services shall be provided by trained engineers/technicians/personnel authorized by Milestone Inc. � Technical support shall be available by telephone as needed within the hours of 8 am � 5 pm. � If parts must be shipped, the Contractor shall provide protective packaging supplies and cover all shipping costs. If parts must be shipped, the Contractor shall cover appropriate protective packaging and shipping costs. Milestone Inc. has been identified as the sole provider for the servicing Original Equipment Manufacturer parts, technical support and contractual maintenance of the UltraWAVE 3 SRC microwave digestion unit. The sole source letter and the quote from Milestone Inc. have been attached. title: Notice of Intent to Sole-Source Award for the Universal Avionics Kapture Golden Chassis
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, AN INVITATION FOR BIDS, OR A REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS. FURTHER, IT DOES NOT REPRESENT A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT TO PAY FOR COSTS INCURRED IN PREPARATION AND SUBMISSION OF DATA OR ANY OTHER COSTS INCURRED IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. This is a Sources Sought Notice with the intent to award a sole source award to APS Aerospace under the authority of FAR 13.106-1 based on APS Aerospace�s unique technical qualifications as the only manufacturer and provider of the Universal Avionics Kapture Golden Chassis as described below. Notice is provided as information to the marketplace, market research, and is an invitation for any other qualified companies to express their interest in and demonstrate their capability to provide the equipment/software that performs the required functions. Background The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is an independent federal agency charged by Congress with investigating every civil aviation accident in the United States and significant events in the other modes of transportation�railroad, transit, highway, marine, pipeline, and commercial space. We determine the probable causes of the accidents and events we investigate and issue safety recommendations aimed at preventing future occurrences. In addition, we conduct transportation safety research studies and offer information and other assistance to family members and survivors for each accident or event we investigate. We also serve as the appellate authority for enforcement actions involving aviation and mariner certificates issued by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and US Coast Guard, and we adjudicate appeals of civil penalty actions taken by the FAA. The NTSB�s Office of Research and Engineering, Vehicle Recorder Division (RE-40) requires the capability to download data from a variety of vehicle recording devices, especially flight data recorders (FDR) and cockpit voice recorders (CVR) from aircraft involved in aviation accidents. These systems require proprietary hardware and software from the manufacturer to download data. The Universal Avionics Kapture download equipment is designed and manufactured by APS Aerospace and is required to download data from undamaged and damaged Universal Avionics Kapture recorders recovered from aircraft involved in accidents investigated by the NTSB. The APS Aerospace product is proprietary and is not sold through any third-party resellers nor is it available for purchase through any government-wide acquisition vehicles. No other commercially available products are available currently that provide the same functionality. The APS Aerospace Universal Avionics Kapture golden chassis and download equipment are considered the definitive method of downloading data from Kapture recorder among industry professionals. Required Capabilities The NTSB requires the Universal Avionics Kapture Golden Chassis. Sources capable of fully satisfying the above requirements are invited to submit capability statements/expressions of interest providing the Government the necessary information to determine actual capability. At a minimum, this information, which must be prepared specifically in response to this notice should, must include: (1) identification of company or organization; (2) an assertion of existing, full capability to meet proposed requirements; (3) business/contracts/marketing office point(s) of contact; (4) notification of business size and/or special status; and (5) any additional information that may be useful to the successful procurement of the requirements, if solicited. These expressions of interest shall adhere to a ten (10)-page submission limit plus web links and any specialized product descriptions. The statement of qualifications should include only information that clearly demonstrates the respondent's capabilities, expertise, and experience to perform the requirements described in this notice. General marketing material should not be included. The NTSB prefers that companies do not submit proprietary material. However, the Government recognizes that proprietary data may be a part of your submittal. If so, clearly mark such restricted or proprietary data and present it as an addendum to the non-restricted/non-proprietary information. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed order based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by NTSB. Parties must submit information within five (5) days of publication of this notice. NTSB will not return capability statements and the supporting documentation submitted in response to this notice. Telephone responses and inquiries will not be accepted. You may email questions regarding this notice to the issuing office to Nicole Evanitsky via email at: nicole.evanitsky@ntsb.gov

title: RCTA Conducting and Documenting Narcotic Investigations
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in the notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number W50S7J26A003 is being issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ) with OPEN MARKET PRICING. This solicitation document, incorporated provisions, and clauses are those in effect through Revolutionary Far Overhaul Federal Effective July 28, 2026, and the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulations (DFARS) Publication Notice (DPN) dated May 07, 2026. This requirement is a small business set aside under NAICS 611699 with a size standard of $16.5M. The MS Army National Guard and the Regional Counterdrug Training Academy (RCTA) have a requirement for Instructional Services for Narcotics Tactical Operations Courses in accordance with the attached Performance Work Statement. The USPFO-MS intends to issue a firm fixed price contract for the courses listed below: CLIN 0001 � Basic Narcotic Investigations CLIN 0002 � Advanced Narcotics Investigation CLIN 0003 � Writing Drug Search Warrants CLIN 0004 � Post Seizure Investigations POP: Sept 2026 � Sept 2027 Exact starting POP will be determined based on award date. Place and Performance of Services: RCTA � 219 Fuller Road, Meridian, MS 39309 and Camp Shelby, Hattiesburg, MS 39402. Remote classes are not authorized. Basis of Award: The government intends to award a firm fixed price contract to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation and is considered to be the most advantageous to the Government in accordance with RFO Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. Evaluation will be in accordance with RFO Subpart 12.2 and is based on Best Value to the Government in terms of (i) Technical capability of the service offered to meet the Government requirement; (i) Price; (ii) Technical . Technical shall be weighted higher than price. To ensure a timely and equitable evaluation of quotes, offerors must comply with the instructions contained herein. Quotes must be complete, self-sufficient, and respond directly to the requirements of this RFQ. Quotes shall include: (1) Price quoted to include itemized description of what is included. (2) detailed specifications and service/course literature that sufficiently describe the service(s) being offered. (3) Date for the 1st class to be held in the month of September. Note: Quotes submitted without detailed specification will not be considered acceptable and shall be removed from further consideration. Quotes are limited to 8 pages including pricing which shall be itemized and information page. This notice does not obligate the Government to award the contract; it does not restrict the government's ultimate approach; nor does it obligate the Government to pay for any quote/proposal preparation costs. Only firm fixed price offers will be evaluated. Along with the quote, please provide company Name with CAGE Code, TIN, UEI and company POC with contact information (email and telephone number). Prompt payment discount terms (i.e. Net 30). SAM is a mandatory requirement for all DoD Government contracts. You must be registered and have an active status in order to be eligible for the award of a contract. To register online go to http://www.sam.gov/. It is the contractors' responsibility to be familiar with applicable Clauses and Provisions. Clauses and provisions incorporated by reference may be accessed via https://www.acquisition.gov/. Please see attached listings of Clauses and Provisions. Questions shall be submitted no later than 2:00 p.m., August 27, 2026. Answers will be posted NLT 4:30 p.m., September 01, 2026. The deadline for receipt of your quote is established no later than 3:30 P.M. Central Daylight Time (CDT), Thursday, September 03, 2026. Please email proposals to ned.mccormick.2@us.af.mil and jared.garner@us.af.mil.

description: The United States Coast Guard is accepting proposals for qualified individuals or firms to replace the roll up doors at Coast Guard MAT Pascagoula. All work is to be completed in accordance with the scope of work/specifications. The scope of work is attached and includes more details of what the Coast Guard needs. Prior to submitting a quote, it is mandatory to examine the scope of work and to visit the facility to make evaluations, etc., and become familiar with existing conditions under which the work will be performed. Site visits are mandatory. Arrangements for visiting the site may be made by contacting: CWO Mike Ackiss Email: Carlton.M.Ackiss@uscg.mil Phone: (504) 239-4937 The work is located at: U.S. Coast Guard MAT Pascagoula 104 USS Vicksburg Way Pascagoula, MS 39595 This will be a firm-fixed priced purchase order awarded to the lowest priced technically acceptable offer. The evaluation factors are: - Price - Technical Acceptability - Past Performance Make sure to provide your price, technical approach, and past performance with your quote. The Government will evaluate the past performance of each offeror to determine the degree of confidence that the offeror will successfully perform the contract requirements. Evaluation will consider the relevance, quality, and timeliness of prior work as demonstrated through submitted references and independent government sources. Offerors with no relevant past performance will receive a neutral rating. Past performance will be rated and factored into the overall evaluation as specified in the solicitation. Offerors, if they wish, can also provide information on problems encountered with the identified contracts and the offeror�s corrective actions. The Government shall consider this information, as well as information obtained from any other sources, when evaluating the offeror�s past performance. The source selection authority shall determine the relevance of similar past performance information. Submit quotes to Alexis.R.Liner@uscg.mil by the date and time listed in this solicitation. This tailoring includes but is not limited to the following: In accordance with FAR Part 36, a quotation is not an offer, and any clause provision to the contrary is hereby modified to be consistent with FAR Part 36. Where the word "offer/offeror" or a derivative of that word appears, it is changed to "quote/quoter" or a derivative of that word. In accordance with FAR 5.101(a)(2), all responsible sources may submit a response which, if timely received, will be considered by the U.S. Coast Guard. This is set aside 100% for small business. Offerors must be actively registered at SAM.gov. Payment and performance bonds are not required.
